overview: Conant Optical is the world's second-largest resin spectacle lens manufacturer by volume (behind Essilor), operating three production bases in Shanghai, Jiangsu (China) and Sabae (Japan), with a fourth under development in Thailand. The Group designs and manufactures standardised, functional and customised corrective lenses sold under its own brand and via ODM/OEM to international ophthalmic companies and retailers in over 90 countries, and since 2023 has been building a second growth leg supplying customised optical lenses and waveguide components for the emerging smart glasses/XR (extended reality) industry. Founder-chairman Fei Zhengxiang is the controlling shareholder; the H shares listed on the HKEX Main Board in December 2021.

business_model.summary: Core revenue comes from manufacturing and selling resin spectacle lenses, split between a higher-margin 'own brand' business (direct sales/branded distribution, ~65% of 2025 revenue, gross margin ~44.7%) and a lower-margin ODM/OEM business supplying global optical brands and retailers (~35% of revenue, gross margin ~36.9%). Lenses are further segmented into standardised, functional/multifunctional (anti-blue-light, photochromic, myopia-control) and customised (high refractive index, premium) products, with customised/functional lines carrying materially higher margins. A fast-growing XR lens segment (smart glasses/AR waveguide optics) emerged from pilot projects in 2023-2024 into commercial revenue in 2025-2026 (H1 2026 XR revenue ~RMB50.5m, up 1,475% YoY from a tiny base) and is explicitly guided by management to become a material growth driver from FY2026.
business_model.customer_type: B2B - international ophthalmic optical companies, spectacle brand owners, retailers/distributors, plus consumer electronics/smart glasses OEMs (e.g., Alibaba's Quark AI glasses program, Goertek, Rokid ecosystem)
business_model.geographic_mix: Overseas ~65% (US, Japan, India, Europe, Australia, Brazil, Thailand) and Mainland China ~35% of FY2025/H1-2026 revenue; China growing fastest (+14-15% YoY) while US/ODM exposure has been dented by US tariffs

main_competitors: EssilorLuxottica (global #1 by volume, ~400m units vs Conant's ~180-206m)
Wanxin Optical / other Chinese standardised lens makers
Goertek Optics, Crystal-Optech, Sunny Optical, Luxshare (in AR waveguide/XR optics)
competitive_position.market_position: Ranked #2 globally by sales volume in traditional resin spectacle lenses (behind EssilorLuxottica) and the only Chinese company among the global top five by sales value; a first-mover among traditional lens makers pivoting into customised XR/smart-glasses lens manufacturing, reportedly the exclusive prescription-lens supplier for Alibaba's Quark AI glasses

moat_factors.description: Three (soon four) global production bases with ~200m+ pieces annual capacity and increasing automation lower unit costs and support large customised orders

moat_factors.factor: Technical/process know-how in high refractive-index and customised lenses
moat_factors.description: Decades of resin lens formulation and coating expertise underpins premium functional/customised product margins (44-55%) versus commodity standardised lenses (~29%)

~3 years of R&D, dedicated Neo Vision XR production line, relationships/JVs with ~20 leading domestic and international smart-eyewear developers (Goertek JV, Rokid investment, Quark supply), a lead that is not yet proven durable given deep-pocketed entrants

moat_factors.factor: Diversified global footprint (China, Japan, soon Thailand)
moat_factors.description: Helps mitigate single-country tariff/regulatory risk and positions supply closer to end customers
Long-standing relationships with international ophthalmic brands and retailers across 90+ countries

weaknesses: Far smaller scale than EssilorLuxottica, which also controls significant downstream retail/distribution that Conant lacks
ODM/OEM segment is commoditised, margin-pressured and directly exposed to US tariff policy

XR business is still small (~3% of FY2025 revenue) and unproven at commercial scale; revenue concentration risk if a handful of marquee XR customer relationships (Quark, Rokid, Goertek JV) underperform

No long-term exclusive contracts disclosed with major XR customers; technology and customer relationships in the nascent AR/VR optics space could be replicated or disintermediated by larger players (Goertek, Luxshare, Crystal-Optech) who are both partners and competitors

growth_drivers: Commercialisation and scaling of XR/smart-glasses lens business - management guides for 'significant growth' in XR sales volume and revenue in FY2026 as several key international customer projects move from trial to mass production
China's 2026 government subsidy scheme for smart glasses (15% rebate, RMB500 cap) expected to accelerate domestic AI/AR glasses penetration and downstream lens demand

Capacity expansion and automation upgrades across Shanghai, Jiangsu (Qidong, Blue Optics), Japan (Sabae) and new Thailand base (six-year BOI tax holiday) to support both traditional and XR volume growth
Product mix upgrade toward higher-margin functional/customised lenses and continued growth of the higher-margin own-brand channel versus ODM

Strategic industrial partnerships/investments - Goertek JV (GoerView) for AR waveguide/electrochromic/eye-tracking components, RMB180m strategic stake in AR unicorn Rokid, 100% consolidation of Jiangsu Blue Optics - aimed at deepening the smart-eyewear supply chain position
Continued geographic diversification of customer base (accelerating growth in Americas ex-US and non-China Asia) to reduce reliance on any single tariff-exposed market

business.description: Early-stage XR revenue is reliant on a small number of marquee programs (Quark, Goertek JV, Rokid-linked projects); delays or loss of any key program would disproportionately hit the growth narrative
ODM revenue fell YoY in FY2025 and customised lens revenue was flat-to-down, explicitly attributed to US tariff impact; further escalation would pressure the lower-margin ODM book
Well-capitalised partners-cum-competitors (Goertek, Crystal-Optech, Sunny Optical, Luxshare) could internalise lens/waveguide capability or outcompete on technology, eroding Conant's first-mover edge
Core resin lens market is large but mature/low-growth outside of mix-upgrade and smart-glasses adjacency; EssilorLuxottica's scale and vertical integration are a structural ceiling on share gains

financial.description: Majority of overseas sales denominated in USD with JPY, EUR exposure also; RMB strength has previously hurt other income and gains (e.g., ~RMB57m FX loss in H1 2026); some hedging (swaps, forwards) in place but not fully eliminating volatility

financial.risk: Large and growing wealth-management/FVTPL investment book
financial.description: RMB1.0bn+ of financial assets at FVTPL (funds/wealth management products) as of H1 2026 introduces mark-to-market and counterparty risk on what is nominally a manufacturing balance sheet

Borrowings roughly doubled H1 2026 (RMB261.6m to RMB639.5m) to fund capacity expansion (Thailand, XR lines); capex increased 138% YoY in H1 2026, requiring continued access to internal cash flow, bank facilities and equity placements
Company has repeatedly funded expansion via share placements (Goertek placement Jan 2025, 27m-share placement Feb 2026 raising ~HK$1.4bn), diluting existing holders even as it funds growth

regulatory.description: Ongoing US-China tariff dynamics directly cited by management as a drag on ODM and customised lens revenue

regulatory.risk: China subsidy policy dependency for smart glasses demand
regulatory.description: Near-term consumer AI-glasses demand in China is partly being pulled forward by a 2026 government subsidy; policy withdrawal or change could soften volume growth
As the smart-glasses category (camera/AI-enabled wearables) scales, evolving privacy/data and product-safety regulation across jurisdictions could affect downstream customer demand

macro.description: Eyewear/smart-glasses purchases carry some discretionary element; a consumer slowdown in key markets (US, China, Europe) could soften volumes

macro.risk: RMB/USD and RMB/JPY exchange rate swings
macro.description: As a majority-export business reporting in RMB with multi-currency costs and revenues, currency volatility materially affects reported margins period to period
Management cited disruptions in raw materials for 1.74-refractive-index lenses in H1 2026 as a headwind to the traditional vision-care business

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Traditional resin spectacle lens industry is large, mature and growing low-to-mid single digits globally, with structural tailwinds from aging populations, rising myopia prevalence (especially in Asia) and premiumisation (functional/customised lenses). The adjacent smart glasses/XR optics market is in an early, fast-growth phase, with brokers (UBS, CICC, Huachuang, Guosen) projecting rapid unit growth driven by major consumer electronics players (Meta, Alibaba, Xiaomi and Chinese AI-glasses entrants) and supported by China's 2026 subsidy program; China is estimated to host over 80% of the smart-glasses supply chain.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate - core eyewear demand is fairly non-discretionary/replacement-driven and resilient, but ODM export orders and the nascent XR revenue stream are more cyclical and customer-program dependent
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low-moderate - modest bank borrowings (debt/equity ~17% as of H1 2026) at fixed rates; capex funded mostly via internal cash flow and equity placements rather than debt

recent_developments.event: Interim dividend of RMB0.20/share approved (up from RMB0.15 in H1 2025) at EGM 21 September 2026; payable by 23 October 2026

H1 2026 results: revenue +7.6% YoY to RMB1,167.1m, gross margin expanded to 42.9% (from 41.0%), net profit +10.4% to RMB301.2m (+27.6% excluding FX); XR revenue of ~RMB50.5m (+1,475% YoY); cash and equivalents more than doubled to RMB1,438.3m following a February 2026 share placement
Completed acquisition of remaining 51% of Jiangsu Blue Optics, taking it to 100% ownership, to expand XR precision-lens capacity
RMB180 million strategic investment (up to 5% stake) in AR unicorn Rokid (灵伴科技), deepening upstream-downstream collaboration in consumer AR glasses
Placed 27,000,000 new shares at HK$52.00/share (~HK$1.4bn raised) to fund XR/Thailand capacity expansion

Asahi Lite (subsidiary) and Goertek Optical formed JV 'GoerView Technology' (Conant 30%/Goertek 70%) for R&D, production and sale of XR waveguide lenses, electrochromic components and eye-tracking optoelectronics

Stock rallied strongly (e.g., +5.5% to HK$56.45 around CES 2026, +10.8% to HK$64.8 in late January) on smart-glasses sector sentiment; multiple broker upgrades/initiations (Citi target HK$70, CICC HK$58, Macquarie HK$88, Morgan Stanley initiated Buy HK$50, UBS initiated Buy, Huachuang Strong Buy HK$63.63, Guosen Outperform HK$61.78-67.96)

FY2025 results: revenue +6.1% to RMB2,186.0m, net profit +30.2% to RMB557.7m, gross margin expanded to 42.0% (from 38.6%); new Neo Vision XR production line and cleanroom commissioned in H2 2025; cash +26.2% aided by Goertek share placement proceeds (6 Jan 2025)
New JV agreement with Goertek Optical and continued progress on Thailand plant (BOI investment certificate obtained, six-year tax holiday)

guidance.as_of: H1 2026 Interim Report (period ended 30 June 2026, published ~August 2026)

items.metric: XR business revenue and sales volume
items.notes: Management states it 'expects its XR business sales volume and revenue to achieve significant growth in the full year of 2026, becoming a new growth driver for the Group in medium- to long term'; no specific numeric target disclosed

items.target: Mass production ramp for key overseas XR customer projects; commissioning of 4 integration/packaging lines in Shanghai; Phase II/III XR line upgrades at Blue Optics (Jiangsu)
items.notes: Qualitative operational milestones rather than financial guidance; two additional international customers expected to move from trial to mass production

items.target: Commence production in 2026 'in an orderly and rhythmic manner'
items.notes: Six-year corporate income tax exemption obtained via BOI certificate from first revenue generated

items.target: Continued elevated capex for automation, XR equipment and Thailand build-out
items.notes: H1 2026 capex already +138% YoY to RMB211.7m (vs RMB88.8m in H1 2025); full FY2025 capex was RMB291.4m (+29.6% YoY)
Up from RMB0.15 per share in H1 2025, approved at EGM 21 September 2026

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman Fei Zhengxiang and management reiterate confidence that the XR/smart-eyewear business will begin contributing 'notable revenue and profit' and become a 'new growth driver' for the Group in the medium-to-long term, framing the Company's strategy as a transformation toward a 'precision optics platform.' Management flags raw-material disruption for 1.74-index lenses and US tariffs as headwinds to the traditional business, partially offset by accelerating China and Americas (ex-US) growth and margin improvement from own-brand/customised mix shift.

bull_case: Early and credentialed leadership position in the fast-growing XR/smart-glasses optics niche, with ~20 customer relationships, a dedicated production line, and marquee programs (reported exclusive Quark AI-glasses lens supply, Goertek JV, Rokid stake) that could scale into a material, high-margin new revenue stream

Core traditional lens business remains the world's #2 by volume with steadily improving margins (gross margin up from 33.9% in 2021 to ~42-43% in FY2025/H1 2026) through mix shift toward own-brand and functional/customised products

Strong balance sheet momentum - cash more than doubled in H1 2026, low leverage, continued profit growth (net profit +30% FY2025, +10%/+28% ex-FX in H1 2026) and a rising dividend, giving flexibility to self-fund capacity expansion (Thailand, Japan, XR lines)

China's 2026 smart-glasses subsidy and broad industry tailwinds (Meta, Alibaba and Chinese consumer electronics players pushing AI glasses) could drive outsized volume growth for lens suppliers positioned early in the supply chain

Strong sell-side sentiment with multiple recent Buy/Outperform initiations and target prices well above several points at which the stock has traded, reflecting optionality the market may still be under-pricing
bear_case: XR revenue remains tiny in absolute terms (~3% of FY2025 revenue) and highly concentrated in a handful of unproven customer programs; commercialisation could disappoint relative to the bullish narrative priced into the stock after its 2026 rally

Stock has shown extreme volatility (swinging from roughly HK$27 to HK$88+ within a 52-week range per some data points), implying high expectations are already embedded and vulnerable to any negative XR news flow or guidance miss
Traditional ODM/customised export business is directly exposed to US tariff policy, which has already dented revenue and could worsen with further trade tensions

Competes and partners simultaneously with much larger, better-capitalised players (Goertek, Luxshare, Crystal-Optech, Sunny Optical) in AR/XR optics, any of whom could internalise capability or win share as the category matures, while EssilorLuxottica dwarfs Conant in the core lens business

Recent dilution (two placements within roughly a year) plus rapidly rising leverage (debt roughly doubled in H1 2026) to fund expansion raises execution risk if XR demand ramps more slowly than the capacity being built out
